work.title: Resolve a stage's skill composition deterministically
work.description: Turn declared manifests into one resolved composition for a stage: exactly one stage skill, required and recommended dependencies, conflict refusal, capability requirements, deterministic ordering, and a resolution digest that is a pure function of the resolved set. Resolution is a read — it reports the selection and the reason for every inclusion and every omission, and writes nothing. Precedence is fixed here: Core invariants, Work state, and repository policy outrank any skill; a secondary skill may add method and may never alter lifecycle decisions or return rules.
acceptance: Resolving a stage yields exactly one stage skill, or refuses with a named error when zero or several would apply
Required dependencies resolve, recommended ones are included or reported as omitted with a reason, and a declared conflict or an unmet capability refuses the resolution
The same inputs always produce the same order and the same resolution digest, and any change to a resolved skill's content changes that digest
A CLI read prints the resolved composition with a reason per included and per omitted skill, and mutates nothing

result.summary: Resolution is a new pure core module: resolveComposition(stage, manifests, hostCapabilities) selects the one stage skill by the codepatrol-<stage> id convention, closes over required dependencies, includes or omits recommended ones with reasons, refuses on conflicts (SKILL_CONFLICT), unmet capabilities (SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET), and zero/several stage matches (SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE), and emits a deterministic order plus a sha256 resolution digest of the resolved set. Manifests gain optional requires/recommends/conflicts under schemaVersion 1; `codepatrol skill resolve <stage>` prints the composition with per-skill reasons and mutates nothing.
result.handoff:
# Plan: Resolve a stage's skill composition deterministically (INIT-1.2)

## Finding (P1)
INIT-1.1 is on main: src/core/skill.ts (schemaVersion 1, strict parser over id/version/kind/capabilities/digest) and `codepatrol skill list` verifying all seven manifests. The manifest declares no dependencies or conflicts yet — this Work adds them additively under schemaVersion 1, so a manifest without the new fields still parses (the "additive later" rule INIT-1.1 set). Core stays filesystem-free; the CLI already owns the skills read via listShippedSkills.

## Product files Build touches
1. src/core/skill.ts — extend SkillManifest, parser, and serializer with optional `requires`, `recommends`, `conflicts`: arrays of unique skill-id tokens (SKILL_ID), each defaulting to absent. schemaVersion stays 1.
2. src/core/skill-resolution.ts (new) — the pure resolver and its types/errors.
3. src/cli/commands/skill.ts — add `skill resolve <stage>` to the existing command.
4. skills/codepatrol-{plan,review,build,verify,ship}/skill.json — add `recommends: ["codepatrol-work"]` (digests are over SKILL.md, so they are unchanged). spec/work manifests unchanged.
5. src/test/skill-resolution.test.ts (new); parser additions covered in src/test/skill.test.ts.

## Resolver (src/core/skill-resolution.ts)
```ts
resolveComposition(stage: Stage, manifests: readonly SkillManifest[], hostCapabilities: readonly string[]): SkillComposition
```
- **Stage selection**: the stage skill is the manifest whose id is `codepatrol-${stage}` (convention, not a new field — nothing to drift). Zero matches or several matches refuse with CodepatrolError SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE naming the stage and the offending count.
- **Closure**: start from the stage skill; iterate to a fixpoint over sorted ids — requires of every included skill must be in the available manifests (a missing required id refuses SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE naming both ends); recommends are included when available, omitted otherwise and reported with the reason "recommended by <id>, not available".
- **Conflicts**: an included skill whose `conflicts` names another included skill refuses SKILL_CONFLICT naming both.
- **Capabilities**: every capability of every included skill must appear in hostCapabilities, else SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET naming the skill and the capability.
- **Order**: the stage skill first, then secondaries sorted by id. Fixed forever.
- **Digest**: sha256 over the canonical JSON of `[{ id, version, digest }]` in that order — a pure function of the resolved set, so identical inputs give identical output and any change to a resolved skill's recorded digest changes the resolution digest.
- Output: `{ stage, skills: [{ id, version, kind, digest }] (ordered), digest, included: [{ id, reason }], omitted: [{ id, reason }] }`. Reasons: "the stage skill for <stage>", "required by <id>", "recommended by <id>".
- The precedence rule from the Work text — Core invariants, Work state, and repository policy outrank any skill; a secondary may add method and never alter lifecycle decisions or return rules — is stated in the module's doc comment. Resolution is selection, not governance.

## CLI read (`codepatrol skill resolve <stage>`)
- Validates the stage argument against STAGES (unknown stage → INVALID_ARGUMENT with usage).
- Resolves over listShippedSkills (package-relative, as today) with the host capabilities the CLI provides: a named constant `HOST_CAPABILITIES = ["cli"]` in the command module — the one capability this host truthfully offers.
- Prints the full composition JSON including per-inclusion and per-omission reasons; mutates nothing; needs no workspace or remote. `skill list` output is unchanged.

## Tests
src/test/skill-resolution.test.ts:
- exactly one stage skill resolves; zero and several each refuse SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE (acceptance 1).
- required dependencies resolve transitively; a missing required id refuses; a recommended skill is included with its reason or reported omitted with its reason; a declared conflict refuses SKILL_CONFLICT; an unmet capability refuses SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET (acceptance 2).
- same inputs twice → identical order and digest; mutating one skill's digest changes the resolution digest (acceptance 3).
- CLI: `skill resolve plan` prints the composition with reasons for codepatrol-plan and the included codepatrol-work, is sorted and idempotent, and an unknown stage refuses (acceptance 4).
src/test/skill.test.ts (extended): parser accepts the new optional fields, refuses duplicates inside them, refuses non-skill-id tokens, and a manifest without them still parses.

## Acceptance coverage
1. Exactly one stage skill or named refusal — id-convention selection + SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE tests.
2. Requires resolve, recommends included/omitted with reason, conflict/unmet capability refuse — closure + error tests.
3. Deterministic order and digest, content-sensitive — digest tests.
4. CLI read with reasons, mutating nothing — `skill resolve <stage>` + CLI test.

## Verification for Build
npm run verify (typecheck, unit tests, smoke, --help showing skill resolve).

## Non-goals
No recording of compositions on runs (INIT-1.4), no evaluation harness (INIT-1.3), no telemetry. No new capability tokens beyond "cli". No precedence enforcement mechanism — documentation only, as the Work fixes precedence in prose here.

traces.message: INIT-1.1 is on main: src/core/skill.ts (schemaVersion 1, strict parser over id/version/kind/capabilities/digest) and `codepatrol skill list` verify all seven manifests. The manifest has no dependency or conflict fields yet — INIT-1.2 must add them additively under schemaVersion 1 (a manifest without them still parses), matching the "additive later" rule INIT-1.1 set. Resolution itself must stay pure like the rest of core; the CLI layer already owns the filesystem read via listShippedSkills.

Resolution design: new pure module src/core/skill-resolution.ts exporting resolveComposition(stage, manifests, hostCapabilities). Stage-skill selection by the id convention codepatrol-<stage> (no new field, nothing to drift); zero or several matches refuse with SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE. The composition is the requires-closure of the stage skill plus present recommends (fixpoint, sorted iteration); a missing required id refuses SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE, a declared conflict refuses SKILL_CONFLICT, a capability outside the host set refuses SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET. Order: stage skill first, then secondaries by id. The resolution digest is sha256 over the canonical [{id,version,digest}] list in that order — a pure function of the resolved set, so any content change moves it. Manifest gains optional requires/recommends/conflicts arrays (unique skill-id tokens) under schemaVersion 1; the five stage skills declare recommends ["codepatrol-work"].

It mutates nothing and touches no workspace. The precedence rule from the Work text (Core invariants, Work state, and repository policy outrank any skill; a secondary never alters lifecycle decisions) is stated in the module's doc comment, not encoded — resolution is selection, not governance.
